rounds.question: Inside eye-level studio, orbitable room, or free exploration?
rounds.answer: yes eye level i think is a good starting point, i think just a 3d room you can looking around is good enough, it should sitll act like a portfolio not like a game
accepted: Portfolio purpose takes priority over game-like exploration.
inferences: Use a fixed viewing position with restrained look controls; no walking controls or game loop.

rounds.question: When someone clicks a project monitor, move closer first, read immediately over the room, or open a case-study page?
accepted: Clicking a project monitor opens readable project content immediately.
No camera move or waiting animation before reading.
inferences: Use a large accessible HTML panel over the room; closing preserves the viewing direction.

state.closure_gate: Interaction tradeoff settled. One material visual-style decision remains because the user explicitly rejected the basic room appearance; it determines modelling, materials and acceptance rather than minor polish.

pending_question.reason: Avoid retaining the rejected basic geometry while only changing camera controls.
pending_question.topic: Richly detailed stylised room versus realistic interior
